fact_fields.method: FCDM (Fully Convolutional Diffusion Model) with ConvNeXt-like backbone

claim_records.text: FCDM-XL achieves competitive performance with 7.5× fewer training steps than DiT-XL/2 at 512×512 resolution while using only 50% of DiT-XL/2's FLOPs.

fact_fields.method: FCDM (Fully Convolutional Diffusion Model) with ConvNeXt-like backbone

claim_records.text: FCDM-XL can be trained on a 4-GPU system, demonstrating exceptional training efficiency of the FCDM architecture.

FCDM-S achieves 48.5 FID after 400K training steps, using 3G FLOPs and reaching 2687 it/s throughput, compared to DiT-S/2's 68.4 FID, 6G FLOPs, and 1234 it/s throughput at the same 400K training steps.

FCDM-B achieves 26.2 FID after 400K training steps, using 12G FLOPs and reaching 1002 it/s throughput, compared to DiT-B/2's 43.5 FID, 23G FLOPs, and 380.1 it/s throughput at the same 400K training steps.

FCDM-L achieves 13.8 FID after 400K training steps, using 48G FLOPs and reaching 381.3 it/s throughput, compared to DiT-L/2's 23.3 FID, 81G FLOPs, and 114.6 it/s throughput at the same 400K training steps.

FCDM-XL achieves 10.7 FID after 400K training steps, using 65G FLOPs and reaching 272.7 it/s throughput, compared to DiT-XL/2's 19.5 FID, 119G FLOPs, and 80.5 it/s throughput at the same 400K training steps.

FCDM-XL achieves 7.9 FID after 1M training steps, using 65G FLOPs and reaching 272.7 it/s throughput, compared to DiT-XL/2's 9.6 FID after 7M training steps, using 119G FLOPs and reaching 80.5 it/s throughput.
When scaled to match DiT model parameter counts, FCDM models require approximately 50% fewer FLOPs than their DiT counterparts.

fact_fields.method: FCDM scalability evaluation following standard DiT training and evaluation framework

claim_records.text: The FCDM architecture follows an Easy Scaling Law defined by only two hyperparameters: number of blocks L and hidden channel C.
FCDM differs from the original ConvNeXt architecture by incorporating conditional injection and being organized in an easily scalable U-shaped design for generative diffusion modeling.
DiC re-examined fully convolutional U-Nets using 3×3 convolutions with sparse skip connections, achieving competitive FID with superior throughput compared to Diffusion Transformers.
DiCo adapted 3×3 separable convolutions and proposed compact channel attention to mitigate channel redundancy, achieving competitive FID with superior throughput compared to Diffusion Transformers.
The proposed FCDM revived ConvNeXt backbone achieves superior generative performance and higher computational efficiency than prior convolutional diffusion models DiC and DiCo.

fact_fields.method: FCDM vs prior convolutional diffusion models comparison

claim_records.text: DiT introduced a fully transformer-based diffusion backbone that replaced convolutions with end-to-end transformer blocks, driving recent state-of-the-art diffusion model success.

claim_records.text: In the ConT block, the patch-wise standard transformer encoder (STE) computes output values for each spatial position from the entire covered area, while the 3×3 stride-2 convolution layer computes only the output value of the center position from the covered area.

Vision transformer models are highly sensitive to training settings including learning rate, number of training epochs, optimizer, and data augmentation, requiring special training configurations or hundreds of millions of images as pretraining datasets.
ConvNets are deficient in large receptive fields due to the locality of convolution, leading to performance degradation on downstream dense prediction tasks.

In ConTNet, a feature-map is split into several patches of the same size, each patch is flattened to a pixel sequence and sent to the STE, then patch embeddings are reshaped back to feature-maps and fed into the next conv layer or STE.

ConvNets are deficient in large receptive fields due to the locality of convolution, leading to performance degradation on downstream dense prediction tasks.

claim_records.text: The routine of the current ViT model is to maintain a full-length patch sequence during inference, which is redundant and lacks hierarchical representation.

Hierarchical Visual Transformer (HVT) progressively pools visual tokens to shrink the sequence length and hence reduces the computational cost, analogous to the feature maps downsampling in Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs).

HVT brings a benefit that we can increase the model capacity by scaling dimensions of depth/width/resolution/patch size without introducing extra computational complexity due to the reduced sequence length.
The average pooled visual tokens contain more discriminative information than the single class token.
With comparable FLOPs, HVT outperforms the competitive baselines on ImageNet and CIFAR-100 datasets for the image classification task.

claim_records.text: Vision Transformers' inherent reliance on sequential input enforces the manual partitioning of images into patch sequences, which disrupts the image's inherent structural and semantic continuity.

Patternformer adaptively converts images to pattern sequences for Transformer input by employing a Convolutional Neural Network to extract various patterns from the input image, with each channel representing a unique pattern that is fed into the succeeding Transformer as a visual token.
By enabling the network to optimize these patterns, each pattern concentrates on its local region of interest, thereby preserving its intrinsic structural and semantic information.
Only employing the vanilla ResNet and Transformer, Patternformer has accomplished state-of-the-art performance on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100.
Only employing the vanilla ResNet and Transformer, Patternformer has achieved competitive results on ImageNet.

claim_records.text: Vision Transformers (ViTs) quickly superseded ConvNets as the state-of-the-art image classification model, initiating the "Roaring 20s" of visual recognition.
A vanilla ViT faces difficulties when applied to general computer vision tasks such as object detection and semantic segmentation.

Hierarchical Transformers such as Swin Transformers reintroduced several ConvNet priors, making Transformers practically viable as a generic vision backbone and demonstrating remarkable performance on a wide variety of vision tasks.
The effectiveness of hybrid ConvNet-Transformer approaches was largely credited to the intrinsic superiority of Transformers rather than the inherent inductive biases of convolutions.
Gradually modernizing a standard ResNet toward the design of a vision Transformer revealed several key components that contribute to the performance difference along the way.

fact_fields.method: Gradually modernize standard ResNet toward vision Transformer design

ConvNeXts maintain the simplicity and efficiency of standard ConvNets while competing favorably with Transformers in terms of accuracy and scalability.

claim_records.text: ConvLLaVA employs ConvNeXt, a hierarchical backbone, as the visual encoder of LMM to replace Vision Transformer (ViT).
ConvLLaVA compresses high-resolution images into information-rich visual features, effectively preventing the generation of excessive visual tokens.
The low-resolution pretrained ConvNeXt underperforms when directly applied on high resolution, so it is updated to bridge the gap as one of the two critical optimizations for ConvLLaVA.

ConvNeXt's original compression ratio is inadequate for much higher resolution inputs, so a successive stage is trained to further compress visual tokens and reduce redundancy as the second critical optimization for ConvLLaVA.
The two optimizations enable ConvLLaVA to support inputs of 1536x1536 resolution generating only 576 visual tokens, capable of handling images of arbitrary aspect ratios.
Experimental results demonstrate that ConvLLaVA achieves competitive performance with state-of-the-art models on mainstream benchmarks.

ConvNeXt's original compression ratio is inadequate for much higher resolution inputs, so a successive stage is trained to further compress visual tokens and reduce redundancy as the second critical optimization for ConvLLaVA.
The two optimizations enable ConvLLaVA to support inputs of 1536x1536 resolution generating only 576 visual tokens, capable of handling images of arbitrary aspect ratios.
Experimental results demonstrate that ConvLLaVA achieves competitive performance with state-of-the-art models on mainstream benchmarks.

claim_records.text: A competitive convolution-free transformer is produced by training on ImageNet only, trained on a single computer in less than 3 days.
The reference vision transformer with 86M parameters achieves top-1 accuracy of 83.1% (single-crop evaluation) on ImageNet with no external data.
A teacher-student strategy specific to transformers is introduced, relying on a distillation token ensuring that the student learns from the teacher through attention.
Token-based distillation, especially when using a convnet as a teacher, leads to results competitive with convnets on ImageNet, where up to 85.2% accuracy is obtained.
Token-based distillation with a convnet teacher also yields results competitive with convnets when transferring to other tasks.

claim_records.text: S2AFormer is an efficient Vision Transformer architecture featuring novel Strip Self-Attention (SSA).
S2AFormer uses Hybrid Perception Blocks (HPBs) to integrate the local perception capabilities of CNNs with the global context modeling of Transformer's attention mechanisms.
Strip Self-Attention (SSA) reduces the spatial dimensions of K and V while compressing the channel dimensions of Q and K.
The SSA design significantly reduces computational overhead while preserving accuracy, striking an optimal balance between efficiency and effectiveness.
S2AFormer is evaluated on ImageNet-1k for image classification, ADE20k for semantic segmentation, and COCO for object detection and instance segmentation.
S2AFormer achieves significant accuracy gains with superior efficiency in both GPU and non-GPU environments.

claim_records.text: A Vision Transformer (ViT) is a simple neural architecture amenable to serve several computer vision tasks.
ViTs have limited built-in architectural priors, in contrast to more recent architectures that incorporate priors either about the input data or of specific tasks.
Recent works show that ViTs benefit from self-supervised pre-training, in particular BerT-like pre-training like BeiT.
The DeiT III supervised training procedure for ViTs builds upon and simplifies a recipe introduced for training ResNet-50.
The DeiT III procedure includes a new simple data-augmentation procedure with only 3 augmentations, closer to the practice in self-supervised learning.

The DeiT III procedure outperforms by a large margin previous fully supervised training recipes for ViT on image classification (ImageNet-1k with and without pre-training on ImageNet-21k), transfer learning and semantic segmentation.
The performance of ViT trained with the DeiT III supervision procedure is comparable to that of more recent architectures.
The DeiT III results could serve as better baselines for recent self-supervised approaches demonstrated on ViT.

claim_records.text: Modern vision systems' performance degrades remarkably quickly when given new tasks with very little data, such as new classes in a classification problem or a domain shift in the input.

Neural network representations underpinning modern vision systems are subject to supervision collapse, whereby they lose any information that is not necessary for performing the training task, including information that may be necessary for transfer to new tasks or domains.
Employing self-supervised learning is proposed as a method to encourage general-purpose features that transfer better, mitigating the supervision collapse problem.

claim_records.text: The feature maps of vision encoders are fundamental to myriad modern AI tasks, ranging from core perception algorithms (e.g. semantic segmentation, object detection, depth perception, etc.) to modern multimodal understanding in vision-language models (VLMs).
The current frontier of general purpose vision backbones in computer vision is Vision Transformers (ViT), typically trained using contrastive loss (e.g. CLIP).
Most off-the-shelf ViTs, particularly CLIP, are inflexibly low resolution, typically running at 224×224px, while their "high-resolution" versions are around 378-448px but still inflexible.

FeatSharp is a novel method to coherently and cheaply upsample the feature maps of low-resolution vision encoders while picking up on fine-grained details that would otherwise be lost due to resolution.
FeatSharp's effectiveness is demonstrated on core perception tasks as well as within agglomerative model training using RADIO as a way of providing richer targets for distillation.

claim_records.text: ViT achieves inferior performance to CNNs when trained from scratch on a midsize dataset like ImageNet.
The simple tokenization of input images in ViT fails to model important local structure such as edges and lines among neighboring pixels, leading to low training sample efficiency.
The redundant attention backbone design of ViT leads to limited feature richness for fixed computation budgets and limited training samples.

T2T-ViT incorporates a layer-wise Tokens-to-Token (T2T) transformation that progressively structurizes images to tokens by recursively aggregating neighboring Tokens into one Token, enabling local structure modeling and reducing token length.

claim_records.text: T2T-ViT uses an efficient deep-narrow backbone structure for vision transformers, motivated by CNN architecture design after empirical study.

methods: Tokens-To-Token Vision Transformer (T2T-ViT) with layer-wise Tokens-to-Token transformation
claims: ViT achieves inferior performance to CNNs when trained from scratch on a midsize dataset like ImageNet.
The simple tokenization of input images in ViT fails to model important local structure such as edges and lines among neighboring pixels, leading to low training sample efficiency.
The redundant attention backbone design of ViT leads to limited feature richness for fixed computation budgets and limited training samples.

T2T-ViT incorporates a layer-wise Tokens-to-Token (T2T) transformation that progressively structurizes images to tokens by recursively aggregating neighboring Tokens into one Token, enabling local structure modeling and reducing token length.
T2T-ViT uses an efficient deep-narrow backbone structure for vision transformers, motivated by CNN architecture design after empirical study.

claim_records.text: Dual Path Network (DPN) is a simple, highly efficient and modularized network for image classification with a new topology of connection paths internally.
ResNet enables feature re-usage while DenseNet enables new features exploration, as revealed by their equivalence within the HORNN framework.
The proposed Dual Path Network shares common features while maintaining the flexibility to explore new features through dual path architectures.
Extensive experiments on ImagNet-1k, Places365 and PASCAL VOC demonstrate superior performance of DPN over state-of-the-arts.
On the ImagNet-1k dataset, a shallow DPN surpasses the best ResNeXt-101(64x4d) with 26% smaller model size, 25% less computational cost and 8% lower memory consumption.
On ImagNet-1k, DPN-131 further pushes the state-of-the-art single model performance with about 2 times faster training speed.
Experiments on Places365, PASCAL VOC detection and PASCAL VOC segmentation datasets demonstrate DPN's consistently better performance than DenseNet, ResNet and ResNeXt over various applications.

claim_records.text: CBNetV2 architecture groups multiple identical backbones connected through composite connections, integrating high- and low-level features of multiple backbone networks and gradually expanding the receptive field for object detection.

Dual-Swin-L achieves 59.4% box AP and 51.6% mask AP on COCO test-dev under the single-model and single-scale testing protocol.

Dual-Swin-L with multi-scale testing achieves 60.1% box AP and 52.3% mask AP on COCO test-dev without using extra training data.
